notes: Provo, UTAH — Utah County seat, pop. 115,162, home to Brigham Young University. 23,133 shipped parcels, $6.71B land value / $18.94B total market value. Source: Utah County's OWN live assessor layer (maps.utahcounty.gov/arcgis/.../Assessor/TaxParcelAll_NoLabel/MapServer/0), clipped to the UGRC Utah Municipal Boundaries polygon for Provo. One row per parcel, 92 fields: geometry + MKT_LAND_VALUE/MKT_IMP_VALUE/MKT_CUR_VALUE + deed ACREAGE + an explicit TAXABLE_CODE + a real use taxonomy. ASMT_YEAR 2027 (the current roll). See run_provo.py.

DO NOT USE UGRC's statewide LIR layer (Parcels_Utah_LIR) for Utah County. This ETL was first built on it — it looks like the ideal one-stop source — and it is SILENTLY MISSING VALUES ON ~20% OF TAXABLE PARCELS. Verified against the assessor's own value history: 4095 W CENTER ST (a 15.9-acre mini-warehouse complex) is NULL in LIR and $6.07M land / $14.0M total at the county; 3581 S MOUNTAIN VISTA PKWY is NULL in LIR and $1.27M land / $9.63M total. Because Utah does not assess exempt land at all, 'no value' reads as 'exempt', so those parcels were being silently DROPPED: the LIR build shipped 18,700 parcels / $5.26B against the county's 23,133 / $6.71B, and downtown University Avenue rendered as a hole (655 parcels / $61.0M in the 200N-600N block, against 917 / $234.3M now). LIR also carries no exemption flag at all for this county. Check value coverage against the county assessor before trusting an LIR sheet for any other Utah county.

VALUES ARE FULL MARKET VALUE, not Utah's 55% primary-residential taxable basis. Verified live against the assessor's own value history for two parcels: MKT_* matches the table headed 'Market Value' row-for-row. TXBL_CUR_VALUE is the reduced taxable figure and is deliberately not used.

LAND VALUE IS INDEPENDENTLY APPRAISED FOR MOST OF THE CITY, BUT FORMULA-ALLOCATED FOR CONDOS/PUDS/SMALL MULTIFAMILY. Utah County publishes real separate MKT_LAND_VALUE / MKT_IMP_VALUE fields (they sum to MKT_CUR_VALUE exactly on all 27,273 taxable parcels), and for Single Family, Commercial, Office, Retail, Industrial and Apartments the land figure genuinely varies — Single Family has 2,719 distinct land values and only 4% sit within 0.5% of the class median. But for several residential classes the assessor allocates land as a FIXED PERCENTAGE OF TOTAL VALUE: CONDO and PUD at 15.55% (97% of them on that exact ratio), IMPROVED CONDOS/PUD at 20%, DUPLEX / FOURPLEX / RES CONVERSION TO APT at 30% (95-96% on the ratio), SUBSIDIZE HOUSING at ~20.6%. Four condos at serial 34068:0001-0004 all read land $46,000 / total $295,800 = 0.15551. For those parcels 'land value per sqft' is total value x a constant / area and carries no independent land signal. That is ordinary mass-appraisal allocation and it is the assessor's own published number, so it ships unchanged (Seattle Westlake precedent) — but it is a real caveat for a land-value map. Scale: 8,355 parcels, 33% of improved parcels, yet only $0.69B of $6.13B improved-parcel land value (11%) — the single-family and commercial land that dominates the map is genuinely appraised. It also explains why merged condo developments calibrate to ~$21/sqft: that is 15.55% of their total value spread over the real site area.

EXEMPTION IS EXPLICIT — the county's TAXABLE_CODE (100 = taxable, everything else an exemption class), not a 'no value' heuristic. 2,840 parcels excluded; the big classes are 959 (BYU, schools, city land — 3,444 acres), 920 (Uinta National Forest sections and the lake flats — 7,433 acres), 998 (ROW) and 600/601 (condo/HOA common area, which the condo merge consumes first). 0 zero-land parcels ship, so Provo has no gp-error layer.
OWNER_NAME is never requested from the source (issue #12) — it does not enter the pipeline at all, rather than being fetched and dropped later.

CONDOS/PUDs ARE MERGED, not hidden (skill §6a/§6b, run_olympia.py recipe). Units are mapped as building-footprint stubs and the county's deed ACREAGE agrees with the stub polygon (median ratio 1.001), so there is no independent land area to fall back on: left alone, CONDO stubs sit at a median $52/sqft and run past $250 against a citywide median of $24. 4,346 unit stubs merge down onto their plat's common-area land -> 206 development parcels at a median $21/sqft, right on the citywide median (the §6b calibration test).

THE MERGE GATE IS PLAT DOMINANCE, NOT ADJACENCY. Utah County serials are MM:PPP:LLLL and MM:PPP is the plat map, so a plat merges only when its sub-2,000-sqft valued stubs are >=60% of its valued parcels. That separates a pure condo/PUD regime (plat 37118: 120 stubs + one 3.9-acre common parcel, zero ordinary lots) from a MIXED subdivision (plat 36196: 8 stubs among 23 valued parcels, the rest ordinary 4,500 sqft townhouse lots at a normal $18/sqft, sharing a 1.07-acre HOA open space). Merging the mixed case would hand the whole HOA open space to 8 units that do not own it — the failure run_lynchburg.py guards against with its 'common-area parcels never chain' rule. Adjacency alone was tried first and got exactly that wrong.

3,209 unit-sized parcels stay individual because NO common-area land is mapped in their plat at all — the development's land is simply absent from the county layer (e.g. 825 N 900 E units 1-6, six 580 sqft stubs and nothing else in plat 55191). There is no key to merge them onto; 290 fall under the sub-500-sqft remnant filter and the rest render hot but bounded (p99 $96/sqft as rendered).

Classification is a direct mapping off the county's own taxonomy (SPC_PROP_TYP_DESCR first — it separates Condo from Townhome from Twin and names parking structures — then PROP_TYPE_DESCR, then ACCOUNT_TYPE for the ~196 DEFAULT records). No heuristics needed. Only 9 parcels land in 'Other'.

Baked to PMTiles + H3 despite being under the ~100k-parcel rule of thumb — small GeoParquet cities render sparse when zoomed out (the Olympia 2026-07-01 lesson), and Provo's condo/townhome stock makes small parcels an unusually large share. Baked with --drop-remnants to match hideRemnants.

Parking is OSM-only but DID classify cleanly: 335 lots / 239.5 acres, split 320 surface / 13 structure / 1 uncertain / 1 excluded. Undercounts like every OSM-only city (the NAIP+ML satellite path was not run), and the county's class scheme has no surface-parking class, so there is no assessor figure to cross-check the undercount against.
